Physics hand-checked: Φ = BA cos θ with θ measured between B and the NORMAL to the surface; flux is a scalar; SI unit weber, 1 Wb = 1 T × 1 m². The book defines flux as the number of field lines through the area — the card uses the quantitative definition the formula needs.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
steps.mark_note: Φ = BA cos θ, with θ named
lines: The magnetic flux Φ through a surface is
the product of the magnetic field B, the
area A of the surface, and the cosine of
the angle θ between B and the normal to
steps.margin_note: First mark. The angle θ is measured from the NORMAL to the surface, not from the surface.
steps.why: cos θ counts only the part of the field that passes straight through the surface; the part parallel to the surface sends no field lines through it.
common_mistakes: Taking θ as the angle between B and the surface. It is measured from the normal to the surface.
Writing Φ = BA for every case. That is the special case θ = 0, field along the normal.

recall.must_convey: That magnetic flux is BA cos θ, with θ measured between the field and the normal to the surface.
accept: field times area times cos theta

steps.memory_tip: Field, area, and the cosine of the angle from the NORMAL — three factors, in that order.

steps.label: Unit and nature
lines: Magnetic flux is a scalar quantity.
Its SI unit is the weber (Wb):

lines.text: Φ = BA cos θ · SI unit: weber (Wb)

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Scalar, and the unit weber with its build-up from tesla and square metre.
steps.why: The flux is the dot product of the field with the area vector, so the result is a single number — a scalar — measured in tesla times square metre, named the weber.
common_mistakes: Calling flux a vector because B is a vector. The dot product of two vectors is a scalar.

recall.must_convey: That flux is a scalar with SI unit weber, equal to tesla times square metre.

steps.memory_tip: Weber = tesla × square metre. Say the unit with its build-up and both facts are covered.

insider_note: The definition mark needs θ tied to the NORMAL of the surface; the second mark is the unit, weber, said with its build-up.
